title: Persistent Memory Skills
description: How to use Gotcha persistent memory under Gotcha/memory.
instructions:
Gotcha persistent memory lives under Gotcha/memory next to chats. SOUL.md is identity and behavior. MEMORY.md is the master map with navigational addresses, never facts. user.md is synced from Settings Personal Info. Detail lives in people/, areas/, notes/ with frontmatter title, area, type, tags, updated. Raw drops (uploads, audio, images, documents in any format) live in raw/.

Session start: SOUL.md and MEMORY.md are already injected as [memory_startup] with absolute paths. Follow them for the whole chat. Load detail files only when the task needs them, with read_file or grep using ABSOLUTE paths. Never resolve memory paths relative to the chat working directory, which is a different folder. Never bulk read the folder.

Link nodes whenever possible: every note, person, area and raw file you create or update must link to the related nodes with Obsidian-style [[links]] (for example [[people/asha-sharma.md]] or [[notes/trip-plan.md]]), and update MEMORY.md so the graph stays connected. One fact in one place: link, never copy-paste content. The viewer draws these links as a node graph, so an unlinked file is an invisible island.

Raw files: when the user shares or uploads a file worth keeping (a voice memo, photo, PDF, receipt, reference doc), save a copy into Gotcha/memory/raw/ with write_file when the content is small enough, and record its absolute path plus a one-line description in the related note and in MEMORY.md. For large files already on disk, do not duplicate them: record the absolute path in place instead. Never store passwords, OTPs, API tokens, or private keys anywhere in memory.

Writes: OPERATOR only with write_file or edit using absolute paths. In MONITOR, read only, never write. Keep SOUL.md under 1500 chars and MEMORY.md under 1500 chars so session start stays cheap.

Areas start as People, Work, Personal, Health. You may rename, add, or archive an area by editing MEMORY.md plus its hub file in areas/. Update MEMORY.md counts and links when you add a note that starts or advances a thread.
